plan.risks: RISK 1: The refusal fails a step with no error_step: until bugs_open/344 lands, the DRIVING work item of a refused edit may be stamped complete by the dispatch loop (the 348/344 shape). Mitigation is inherent, not procedural: the live page is untouched (the write never happens) and the required_fields_missing item is filed BEFORE the refusal, so the defect is on the queue regardless of the driving item's status. 344 owns the completion fix; this round deliberately does not touch it. RISK 2: The armed refusal changes edit outcomes: an edit that today persists a blank required field will fail once 551 applies. That is the intended authority change and it is opt-in — 551 is the visible act, on the one live consumer, after the roll. The seam judges the MERGED map (fleet defaults included), so it fires only when the field would genuinely render empty — a strict subset of the writer-side gate's population (pinned by TestSeamReportsASubsetOfThePreRenderGateAndSaysWhy). RISK 3: Arming the chrome record could flood the queue if the population were misjudged: measured 0 rows fire today, and the emitter co-dedups with the post-deploy check on the shared item_key shape, so even future firings converge on one item per page/slot. RISK 4: The unit tests cannot see a branch that stops copying AbsentRequiredFields onto the outcome (needs a DB): stated in the test comment, covered by the post-roll canary in 551's header — one refusing edit (live section byte-identical) and one clean edit (persists) in the same run. RISK 5: 550's dynamic loop writes to every step carrying the action, including any added between review and apply: that is the intent (the key is the policy for the ACTION's chrome surface), and the post-verify asserts the invariant over the live set at apply time rather than over a stale enumeration.
